decision_table.name: Determine_IN_Filing_Requirement
decision_table.description: Determine if corporation must file Indiana state corporate tax return. Checks for physical presence or economic nexus.

condition.name: has_physical_presence
condition.comment: Has physical presence in IN (office, employees, property)

actions.action: // Physical nexus established - filing required // Apportionment will be calculated by tables 7000-7500

rule.policy:
IN filing required due to physical presence (office, employees, or property in state).
A corporation has physical presence nexus in IN if it has: - An office, store, warehouse, or other place of business in IN - Employees working in IN - Tangible personal property located in IN - Real property located in IN
Reference: Indiana Code § 6-3-2-2 (Nexus and apportionment) Reference: Indiana Department of Revenue Directive #35 (Nexus standards)

actions.action: // Economic nexus established per Wayfair - filing required // Apportionment will be calculated by tables 7000-7500

rule.policy:
IN filing required due to economic nexus (post-Wayfair).
Economic nexus threshold: $100,000 gross receipts in IN.
As of January 1, 2024, Indiana eliminated the 200-transaction threshold, simplifying compliance by focusing solely on revenue volume.
Effective January 1, 2019, Indiana taxes corporations "to the fullest extent permitted by federal law" regardless of physical presence, following South Dakota v. Wayfair, Inc., 138 S. Ct. 2080 (2018).
The $100,000 calculation includes all gross receipts from Indiana sales— both taxable and exempt transactions.
Reference: South Dakota v. Wayfair, Inc., 138 S. Ct. 2080 (2018) Reference: Indiana Department of Revenue Remote Seller Information Reference: Indiana Code § 6-2.5-2-1 (Economic nexus provisions)

No IN nexus - no filing requirement.
Corporation does not meet physical presence or economic nexus thresholds. Any estimated payments would be refunded.
Reference: Indiana Code § 6-3-2-2 (Nexus requirements)

decision_table.name: Calculate_IN_Income_Adjustments
decision_table.description: Calculate IN state-specific additions and subtractions to federal taxable income.

condition.name: has_nexus
condition.comment: Must have nexus to calculate adjustments

rule.policy:
IN state-specific income adjustments to federal taxable income.
IN ADDITIONS to federal taxable income include: - Interest income from obligations of states other than Indiana or their political subdivisions (if acquired after December 31, 2011) - State income taxes deducted on federal return - Expenses related to exempt income - Certain other state-specific adjustments
IN SUBTRACTIONS from federal taxable income include: - Interest on Indiana state and municipal bonds - Indiana net operating loss deduction (subject to IN limitations) - Certain dividend income - Certain refunds of state income taxes
Note: Interest earned from Indiana municipal obligations is not taxable for Indiana income tax purposes. However, interest from out-of-state municipal bonds acquired after December 31, 2011, must be added back.
Indiana continues to require business interest expense to be deducted in the current year the interest is paid or accrued (conformity to IRC § 163(j)).
Reference: Indiana Form IT-20 Schedule A (Additions to Federal Taxable Income) Reference: Indiana Form IT-20 Schedule B (Subtractions from Federal Taxable Income) Reference: Indiana Department of Revenue Income Tax Information Bulletin 19 Reference: Indiana Code § 6-3-1-3.5 (Adjustments to federal taxable income)

No nexus - no state adjustments calculated.
Corporation does not have IN nexus, so no income adjustments are needed.

decision_table.name: Calculate_IN_State_Tax
decision_table.description: Calculate IN state corporate income tax. Applies IN 4.9% flat rate to apportioned and adjusted taxable income.

condition.name: has_nexus
condition.comment: Must have nexus to owe tax

rule.policy:
IN state corporate income tax calculation:
1. Federal taxable income: [Form 1120 line 28] 2. Apportioned to IN: × [IN apportionment percentage] 3. IN additions: + [Out-of-state municipal interest, state taxes, etc.] 4. IN subtractions: - [IN municipal interest, IN NOL, etc.] 5. IN taxable income: = [Result] 6. IN tax rate: × 4.9% flat rate 7. IN income tax: = [Tax before credits] 8. IN credits: - [Economic development, R&D, HQ relocation, etc.] 9. IN tax liability: = [Final tax]
IN uses single-sales factor apportionment (100% sales factor).
IN tax rate: - 2025: 4.9% flat rate - Indiana is among thirteen states with corporate tax rates at or below 5%
IN provides various tax credits including: - Economic Development for Growing Economy (EDGE) Credit - Research Expense Tax Credit - Headquarters Relocation Tax Credit - Neighborhood Assistance Credit - Venture Capital Investment Tax Credit
Indiana conforms to the Internal Revenue Code as of January 1, 2026, per Senate Bill 243 (2025), with certain notable exceptions.
Reference: Indiana Form IT-20 (Corporation Income Tax Return) Reference: Indiana Code § 6-3-2-1 (Tax rate of 4.9%) Reference: Indiana Code § 6-3-2-2 (Single-sales apportionment) Reference: Indiana Department of Revenue Corporate Tax Guidance 2025

No IN nexus - no tax liability.
Corporation does not have physical presence or economic nexus in IN. Any estimated payments are refunded.
Reference: Indiana Code § 6-3-2-2 (Nexus requirements)

No IN taxable income - no tax liability.
Corporation has IN nexus but no positive taxable income after apportionment and adjustments. Any estimated payments are refunded.
IN net operating loss (NOL) rules may apply: - IN allows NOL carryforward consistent with federal rules - NOL deduction limitations apply similarly to federal treatment
Reference: Indiana Form IT-20 (Corporation Income Tax Return) Reference: Indiana Code § 6-3-2-2.6 (Net operating loss deduction)
